name: Vacuum pose

lead: The vacuum pose is a bodybuilding pose where the competitor exhales, pulls the navel in toward the spine and expands the ribcage, so the waist looks small and the chest and lats look wider. It is used by physique competitors and by people posing for photos who want a tapered look.

It is built on the stomach vacuum, a technique that mainly uses the transverse abdominis. Forum members describe it as a skill that improves with practice and with muscle, and as a staple of classic bodybuilding that has returned in classic physique divisions. No research examines it as a posing technique.

paras: Lifters practise it in front of a mirror or on camera, often as part of posing sessions before a contest, and some combine it with chest expansion exercises. Many practise it on an empty stomach, and the pose is usually held briefly.

The pose carries few direct risks, though Wikipedia notes that performing a vacuum while bending or lifting heavy weights is disputed. Forum members also note that it looks best with muscle mass and conditioning behind it.

angle.text: The pose shrinks the apparent waist and exaggerates the chest and lats. People use it to show a tapered physique in competitions and photos.

lead: The vacuum pose is a bodybuilding pose in which the competitor draws the abdomen inward and lifts the ribcage to make the waist appear much narrower and the torso more tapered. It is used on stage and in physique photos. [1][2]

Its mechanism is the stomach vacuum, which pulls the navel toward the spine by contracting the internal abdominal muscles, mainly the transverse abdominis, and is used in bodybuilding competitions to make the stomach look flatter. [1] Forum users on T Nation describe it as a classic-era pose that has returned in classic physique divisions. [3][3]

paras: The stomach vacuum draws the navel in by contracting the deep abdominal muscles, mainly the transverse abdominis and less so the diaphragm. In the vacuum pose this is combined with a lifted chest so the abdomen looks hollowed. [1]

Forum members discuss the pose in the context of contest preparation and physique critique; one T Nation user advised a competitor to develop a Zane-style vacuum pose before a show, and another said it earns points from judges. [4][5] Another forum user observed in 2019 that the pose was back after the classic division rose at the Mr. Olympia. [3]

Posters differ on its history: one said people stopped using it because chest expansion exercises fell out of fashion, while others describe it as the kind of pose that looks best on someone with muscle. [6][7]
Wikipedia notes that whether vacuuming while bending or lifting heavy weights is beneficial or healthy is disputed. [1]
